newsitem.title: UK: Hanson shareholders approve final demerger.
newsitem.headline: Hanson shareholders approve final demerger.

text.p: Shareholders in Anglo-US building services and energy group Hanson Plc on Friday voted overwhelmingly in favour of its final demerger -- that of its Energy Group, which is to be spun off on February 24.
A company spokeswoman told Reuters at a shareholders meeting called to consider the move that 98 percent of shareholders had approved the demerger and a share consolidation.
The demerger will give shareholders one Energy share for every 10 existing Hanson shares held, and so-called grey market trading has already begun in both Energy and the new

Asked whether there might be a further sub-demerger of the two main components of the Energy Group, U.S.-Australian Peabody Coal and Britain's largest regional electricity company Eastern, group chairman and founder Lord Hanson said he thought not.
"No, I have had enough of demergers and I think (the two) fit very well together," he replied to a shareholder question.
Energy, to be listed in London and New York, has said it is already mulling a string of acquisitions in Britain and North America and has started talks with a US power marketing company.
Hanson's first two demergers, of Britain's Imperial Tobacco and U.S.-quoted Millennium Chemicals, took place last October.
